title: Degreewise section products identify localized external cochains with independent coefficient universe
statement: For a ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] with commutative ring sheaf R, an object U, and arbitrary integer-indexed module-sheaf cochain complexes L,I [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], let S be the abelian-group complex of sections at U of their sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], res restriction to U, and π the projections chosen in homComplex_exists. There exist additive equivalences e_n from S.X n to the external degree-n cochains between res L and res I for every integer n. For each x,p,q with p+n=q and localized object W, the component (e_n x).v p q at W is the evaluated projection π(L,I,n,p,q) applied to x, evaluated at W. This asserts degreewise products only, with no cycles, boundaries, cohomology or homotopy-category maps. This universe-general form takes C : Type u with Category v and coefficient/module universe max u v r, for arbitrary r; assume abelian-group sheafification and its locally bijective characterization on the original site. It uses the same sheaves, restriction, Hom complex, differentials, and induced maps as the original source statement.

proof.text: Work with objects in Type u, arrows in Type v, and coefficient rings and modules in Type (max u v r). Use the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances on the slice whenever an abelian or exactness instance is needed. All these instances are proved, and the given base-site instances are retained.

Apply product preservation to the chosen fan in homComplex_projections_exists: forgetting module sheaves, evaluating at U, and forgetting modules to abelian groups preserve the integer-indexed product. Its evaluated projections identify degree-n sections with the product of internal Hom sections at U.

By the construction of internal Hom, each factor is the group of presheaf-module maps on C/U. The fully faithful forgetful functor on localized module sheaves identifies it with the group of localized sheaf-module maps. Families indexed by p are external degree-n cochains; q is transported along p+n=q. The product universal property gives inverse maps, proves addition preservation and the displayed projection formula.
